Maybe you are not familiar with programming languages, because this is not a command, it is an RGSS variable.
In the line that checks the SWITCH, he used it by calling the variable that is in the module, that is, this way the developer does not need to look for in the SCRIPT where to define the numerical ID:
If you don't use this, the game developer will need to find the line, which is 906, and modify the numeric ID to the desired value, for example "$game_switches[100]".

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
First, you can never disable an entire script while the engine is running, only functions of a script and only if they were prepared to be disabled.
Think of it like working on the engine of your car. You cannot do it while driving on the highway at 50 km per hour, but if someone installed a switch in the cockpit then you can turn that to change something while driving.
However, like with installing a switch in your car it will only work if the one doing the install knows what he/she is doing.
For example if the script makes changes to the savefiles to save its own data, then you need to keep those changes no matter what is switched - which means you cannot have the switch over the entire scripßt but only over part of the script.
If you would make the switch over the entire script, the savefiles would become incompatible the second the switch turns off the part that modifies the savefiles.
